title: the phase overhead and the task cycle cost less with every guarantee kept
desiredOutcome: the phase overhead falls inside its 1.00 budget in every benchmark session, and the per-task cycle moves toward 1.25 times plain like for like, each lever confirmed by its offline micro-test before any paid session

tasks.title: the remaining cost is located per step and each lever is designed with its micro-test

outcome.technical:
Locates the cost that remains after P118, per step, and designs four levers, in the new docs/research/pipeline-cost-levers.md. Every figure there sits beside the command in its section 8.

stream-cost:
- load_streams() reads several streams of one session in one call. They must share the same session id and be given in order; otherwise the call is refused with exit 2.
- unheld_reads() and main() refuse a follow-up stream read alone with exit 2, when modelUsage's cache reads exceed what the stream can hold.
- The mispricing was 18081 x (8.0-5.0)/1e6 = 0.054243.
- Over every recorded stream under the experiments directory, only the follow-up alone is refused. Every other report is byte-identical to HEAD; this was run twice, about 20 minutes apart.
- Cases sc30-sc34. sc30, sc31, sc33 and sc34 failed on the unfixed code, and the allow twin sc32 passed.
- The orchestrator re-ran the mutation probe (scratchpad p119-1/mutations.py): nine mutations, all red on their target cases, including three over-fire rows that turn sc32 red.

pipeline-cost-results.md has three in-place corrections:
- a pointer to the instrument fix;
- the one-line hand-back estimate, re-derived with the CLI frame as 1.254 / 1.333 / 1.189;
- cost-C-2 re-derived as 1.224.

Findings:
- The phase overhead per step: the driver's sign-off call runs in 2.4-2.6 s, and its model cost is the sign-off answer request.
- The phase review value test: verdict clean with no findings in each session, every task `matches`, and no file outside docs/audit changed after the review. A computed fact, "an existing test file was modified", matched the grader's protected flag in all three sessions; the reviews' readings did not.
- The executor hand-back costs 0.0504 / 0.0593 / 0.0557 a cycle.
- CLAUDE.md is 2193 B in each agent start, and omitClaudeMd is not recommended.

Levers:
- A: the plan batch on stdin.
- B: submit prints the hand-back instruction last.
- C: the sign-off answered in advance, applied only when it is the triage's single admissible answer.
- D: the review's mechanical answers computed, with the existing-test fact added to the phase brief.

Predicted phase overhead 0.5653 / 0.5501 / 0.7096, at most 0.8267 with each estimate taken adversely. Predicted per task 1.254 / 1.333 / 1.189.

Not recommended: a SubagentStop block hook, which costs more than it saves. The review on a signal or off was put to the user, who chose to keep it, narrowed.

red-first: the helper is could-not-prove, because the task declares no test file. The pre-fix run recorded 44/48 with the four deny cases red.

Faults recorded internally: the own-tests command in the executor brief, the --introduces symbol, and the CLI frame in the hand-back apportioning.
outcome.descriptive: The cost left after the last phase is measured step by step, and four changes are designed that should bring the phase overhead under budget in every measured session; the cost tool now prices a resumed session correctly.

outcome.technical:
Lever A. `audit-task.py add --from-file -` reads the planning batch from stdin.

How it reads:
- read_batch(path, stream=None) takes the batch from _batch_from_file or _batch_from_stdin.
- Either way it is graded by the same batch_problems(), then the same single lock, write, revalidation from disk and rollback.
- An empty stdin is refused as empty.
- The refusal header names "the batch on stdin".

What changed outside the verb:
- commands/phase.md's add section shows `add --from-file - <<'PLAN'` with the plan as its body, and the Write-tool step is gone. The section measures 3974 -> 3962 bytes by `tools/measure-context.py --gate`, under the run form's 4000 ceiling.
- reference/verbs-in-full.md shows the heredoc form, says to quote its word, and lists an empty stdin as a refusal.
- CHANGELOG: one line under [Unreleased].

Cases (all in test_audit_task.py):
- fb10: the add section pins the heredoc.
- fb13: a file batch and the same batch on stdin give byte-identical plans, with the request and the open choices kept.
- fb14: a malformed batch and an empty stdin are each refused, and the plan's bytes are unchanged.
- fb15: phase.md's own heredoc command, run through sh, writes the same plan; the context gate still reports OK.
- fb16: every hook hooks.json routes Bash to refuses nothing for the heredoc. Its over-fire control is guard-secrets-read denying `cat .env`.

Red-first: proved, on fb10 and fb13-fb16 at HEAD.

Mutation probe (scratchpad P119.2-g0k/mut.py), re-run by the orchestrator: exit 0, baseline green, all 7 rows KILLED with exactly their expected cases.

Left: the `[--from-file PATH]` hints in commands/task.md and README.md, which are still true but do not mention `-`.
outcome.descriptive: Planning a phase now passes its plan straight into the add command, so no scratch file is written that could be refused or collide, and the request and its open choices are always saved.

tasks.title: a clean phase review is signed off in the same call that files it
tasks.description: Lever C of docs/research/pipeline-cost-levers.md, section 6. At the phase reviewer's dispatch, the driver also prints the call to send after it: `next <phase> --answer sign-off --reason <the summary>`. That answer applies only when the triage has sign-off as its single admissible answer: review clean, no finding open, no answer waiting on a human, no fix task after its head. Otherwise the triage prints as today and the answer is reported as not applied. The sign-off verb, gate, invariants, commit, landing and lock release run unchanged. Micro-test as listed: a clean review answered in advance signs off and prints done in one call; with a finding open, or an answer waiting on a human, the same call prints the triage and runs no sign-off; stream-cost's driven-span cases still place the landing in the close. CHANGELOG under [Unreleased] gets one line for lever B (the hand-back print) and one for this. Every case is shown red first.

outcome.technical:
Lever C. The phase reviewer's dispatch now prints a second line: `then: next <phase> --answer sign-off --reason <the summary>`.

drive() takes `--answer sign-off` with no decision pending as an answer in advance only when advance_admissible holds: every task terminal and the phase not yet signed off. Everywhere else, `no decision is pending` still refuses.

At the triage, advance_applies decides. It holds only for a filed review with verdict `clean`, no finding open, no answer waiting on a human, and no fix task closed after the review's head. That is exactly the state in which the triage refuses every other answer. Then the normal sign-off path runs, unchanged: the phase gate, invariants, signoff verb, commit, landing and lock release. Otherwise the triage prints as before, with "not applied", and when no triage was reached, the call says so.

The phase loop moved unchanged into drive_phase(). CHANGELOG [Unreleased] gets one line for lever B and one for lever C.

Cases, in sg-block:
- sq0: the advance call is still refused mid-phase.
- sq1: the dispatch prints the call once.
- sq2: a clean review signs off and lands in one call.
- sq3: with a finding open, the call does not sign off.
- sq4: with an answer waiting on a human, the call does not sign off.
- sq5: with a fix task closed after the review's head, the call does not sign off. Added at the orchestrator's request, because that term guards a diff no review saw.
- sq3m and sq0m: in-suite red mutants.

Red-first: proved (sg-block at HEAD 13/19, the task's cases red). sq5 was added after that and is inferred red at HEAD (E_USAGE), not observed.

Mutation probe (scratchpad P119.4-g0k/mut.py), re-run by the orchestrator: exit 0, every row killed, including drop-fixes-after, which only sq5 catches.

stream-cost's driven sign-off case sp14 still passes.

Suite time: 217 s before the change on a quieter machine, 277 s after at load 15-17. The new cases took about 14 s, measured twice. P119.7 takes the suite's runtime.
outcome.descriptive: When the phase review comes back clean, the one call the main session is told to send signs the phase off and merges it; with anything open, that call shows the choices instead and signs nothing.

The intent answer stays the reviewer's, and the sign-off verb still refuses until every owed task has one. Every case is shown red first.

tasks.title: the executor brief prints a test command that can run
tasks.description: Internal fault, measured by the levers analysis. The executor brief prints `run-test-gate.py ... --own --quiet` while the same brief says no gate entry names the task's tests.add file, so the executors' own-tests runs printed 'no gate entry' or rc=2 three times in each arm C session: wasted requests in the cycle. Print the own-tests command only when a gate entry selects the task's tests; otherwise print the suite command the brief already names for the task's test file. tasks.title: the driver's suite runs well inside the sweep's per-file cap
tasks.description: Internal fault, measured twice in this phase. On its own, plugins/audit/tests/test_drive_phase.py --selftest takes about 217-231 s on a quiet machine, and 277 s was observed under load. tools/sweep-selftests.py caps each file at 300 s, so a loaded gate can time the file out and read a sound change as red. Find where the suite's time goes by profiling the stages; the likely shape is a real git fixture repo built per case. Cut the time by sharing fixtures across cases that only read them, or by building a fixture once per stage and copying it, without changing what any case asserts. Every case id keeps its name and its verdict. Report the per-stage time before and after, measured twice with a gap, and the whole-file time. The cap is not raised, and the 1:1 test-file rule (one tests/test_<module>.py per module) is kept, so the suite is not split into new files. A mutation that breaks a shared fixture must still turn the cases that read it red; show one.
